# The narrowings of the bench-name rule (internal/ci/benchname_class_test.go).
#
# THE RULE (Glenn's lock, 2026-09-18): runner hosts are CI-only. A function taking a bench
# NAME must resolve it through the machines registry (internal/fleet) before that name
# reaches a machine. These are the functions that do not, and why each one is a narrowing
# and not a hole. One entry per line: <path>:<func> then the reason. The list only shrinks:
# a function that has left, or that resolves its name now, is a red run.

internal/pulse/manager.go:reissue formats the requeued card's text and touches no machine; the bench it names is written into a card that pulse.Fill resolves before launching it
internal/pulse/fill.go:writeLaunchedMarker writes the launched card's marker on the coordinator's own disk and touches no machine; the bench it records is the one pulse.Fill already put through refuseNonBenches and guardedLauncher before the card was launched at all

# `harvest --bench` resolves its name ONCE, at the verb's edge: harvestBench calls
# requireBench (fleet.Registry.RequireBench) before the first ssh. These four are below
# that guard and are reached through nothing else.
internal/pulse/harvestbench.go:prTitle formats one harvested job's PR title and touches no machine; the bench is a word in the title's suffix
internal/pulse/harvestbench.go:benchPRBody formats the PR body and touches no machine; the bench is a word in the provenance line
internal/pulse/harvestbench.go:benchRepoURL builds the ssh://<bench><dir>/repo string the LOCAL clone fetches from; it opens nothing, and the name it formats is the one harvestBench's requireBench guard let past
internal/pulse/harvestbench.go:markHarvested one `touch <dir>/.harvested` through the BenchShell seam, called only from harvestBench after its requireBench guard; the seam below it is sshShell.Run
internal/pulse/harvestbench.go:sshShell.Run the raw ssh seam; the same road as cmd/nova-pulse's sshCapacity.Capacity -- it is constructed in exactly one place (harvestBench, when the caller injected no BenchShell) and reached only through that verb, which resolved the bench name first

cmd/nova-pulse/fill.go:sshCapacity.Capacity the raw ssh capacity probe; it is reached only through pulse.Fill, which wraps every Capacity in guardedCapacity and asks RequireBench first, and it is constructed in exactly one place (cmd/nova-pulse/fill.go) and handed straight to pulse.Fill
cmd/nova-pulse/fill.go:flashLauncher.Launch the raw per-card launcher; the same road, wrapped by pulse.Fill in guardedLauncher, constructed in exactly one place and handed straight to it
cmd/nova-pulse/fillstore.go:storeProbeConfig.probe the slot-store capacity probe (#1914); the same road as sshCapacity.Capacity -- it is the Probe seam of pulse.StoreCapacity, which pulse.Fill wraps in guardedCapacity and asks RequireBench first, and it is constructed in exactly one place (cmdFill) and handed straight to pulse.Fill
cmd/nova-pulse/fillstore.go:storeProbeConfig.runProbeOverSSH the ssh half of that probe, reached from storeProbeConfig.probe and from nothing else, below the same guard
internal/pulse/fillstore.go:StoreCapacity.Capacity the pulse.Capacity the fleet runs on; pulse.Fill wraps EVERY Capacity in guardedCapacity, which asks fleet.Registry.RequireBench before the name reaches this call, and this function starts no child of its own -- its injected Probe does

cmd/nova-pulse/power.go:powerOnlineCount the Mac power verbs exist FOR the CI runner hosts: nova-pulse wake and sleep are how batman and superman are woken for the merge group and let sleep again (the fleet runs on solar). A runner host is the RIGHT answer here, so a bench guard would refuse the verb's whole purpose; they place no card and no load, only a magic packet and a runner-list read
cmd/nova-pulse/power.go:powerBusyCount the same verbs, asking GitHub whether that runner host's runners are busy before letting it sleep
cmd/nova-pulse/power.go:powerWakeFail formats one WAKE FAIL line for those verbs and touches no machine
